title: Moderation Systems — OpenAI, Perspective, Llama Guard

questions.question: What happens when run receives "how do i make a bomb"?
options: input_moderator flags illicit/violent at 0.9 and returns a refusal before model_respond runs
Only the custom financial rule runs and the model answers
The output moderator waits for a generated answer before deciding
The prompt is rewritten as a C2PA manifest
questions.explanation: CATEGORY_TRIGGERS maps bomb to illicit/violent with score 0.9, above the default 0.5 threshold. run returns from the input layer, so no model output or output-layer check is produced for that prompt.

questions.question: What does the custom_domain_rules branch add for "should i invest in memecoins"?
options: A hate-category score
A financial-advice refusal and a non-fiduciary disclosure
A Llama Guard 14-category result
A prompt-injection exploit
questions.explanation: The general moderation map has no finance trigger. custom_domain_rules catches the phrase and returns the explicit financial-advice message before generation, showing why domain rules complement broad classifiers.

questions.question: Why is output_moderator still needed when input_moderator already passed?
options: The output layer is the only layer that can parse Python
Input moderation always runs after generation
Output moderation changes the model's weights
Outputs can contain hallucinated or bypassed harmful content that was not present in the user's input
questions.explanation: run checks input, custom rules, then generation, and finally applies the same category scoring to output. The output layer catches failures introduced during generation or by an evasion that input inspection missed.

questions.question: What is Perspective API primarily used to score in the lesson?
options: Watermark provenance
Token-level privacy leakage
Reward-model KL divergence
Toxicity dimensions such as severe toxicity, insult, profanity, threat, and identity attack
questions.explanation: Perspective is presented as a pre-LLM-era toxicity baseline with several sub-dimensions. It can be useful for research comparisons but is not a complete modern multimodal or domain-policy stack.

questions.question: How does OpenAI's omni-moderation taxonomy differ from the toy CATEGORIES list?
options: The production schema expands top-level families into 13 text/image categories and subcategories, while the toy collapses them to eight
The production endpoint has no categories and returns only a string
The toy has more categories than any production API
They are identical, including every threatening and instruction subcategory
questions.explanation: The code deliberately collapses subcategories such as harassment/threatening and self-harm/instructions. The lesson distinguishes that pedagogical map from the 13-category omni-moderation response schema.

questions.question: What migration does the lesson specify for Azure Content Moderator?
options: Migrate to Perspective API before its 2024 shutdown
Migrate to Azure AI Content Safety before retirement on 15 March 2027
Remove all output moderation after February 2024
Replace it with C2PA metadata
questions.explanation: The timeline in the lesson says Content Moderator was deprecated in February 2024 and retires on 15 March 2027. Azure AI Content Safety is the stated migration target, not a provenance system.
